starts.name: Arrive at Liscor
starts.intro: You stand outside the east gate of Liscor, a walled city of Drakes and Gnolls.

starts.name: Arrive at Celum
starts.intro: You stand outside the gate of Celum, a walled Human city north of the High Passes.

tactical.note: M17.0 (ADR 0027). XCOM-style rounds, the user's AP rules (ADR 0022). AP in quarter points (q): 6 AP = 24 q, one tile = 1 q. M17.1 reads it (core/encounter.gd); M17.2 turns it on and adds initiative.npc_default (all NPCs, own numbers in M17.7). hp_scale is set in M17.7 (paper fights suggest 2.0).

cover.note: M17.6 (ADR 0027). Points taken off a ranged hit chance by cover on the tile next to the target (half, full; a wall counts as full when the shooter still sees the target). flank = points ADDED when the target has fighters of the attacker's side on two opposite tiles. sight: walls block throws, shots and targeted spells. kinds: the cover level of a solid object by its kind (a map object may set its own cover). All numbers are design guesses; melee ignores cover.

portal.note: M10.0 (ADR 0017). The Albez door. Before Erin's [Magical Grounds] (Level 30, 3.33) it has almost no mana, so its power_flags keep it shut to the player. After that the book gives about 16-30 people a day for everyone; the player's share is a design number. A trip is instant in the text; one minute here so it is a travel action.
portal.line: You step through the door and come out in %s.
portal.dry_line: The door opens onto a blank wall. It has no mana to spare.
portal.spent_line: The door opens onto a blank wall. It has carried enough people for today.

traps.note: M13.T (ADR 0020). The trapped rooms of Liscor's dungeon (4.08 T, 4.19). The chances and damage are design numbers. A search takes 10 minutes and checks every hidden trap within search_radius tiles.
traps.search_name: The floor and walls around you
traps.disarm_fail_line: It goes off in your hands: %s!
traps.blocked_line: %s is there. Disarm it or go around.

cold.line: The cold bites through your clothes. (-%d HP)
cold.morning_line: Winter has come. Outdoors the cold wears you down: stay indoors or by a fire.

fairies.name: Frost Fairy
lines: Stop gawping, mortal. Ye look like a frozen fish.
Away with ye! This field is ours till the thaw.
Hah! Another lost one who can see us. How dull.
Yer nose is going blue. It suits ye.
Talk, talk, talk. Mortals never learn to be quiet.
We could bury ye to the chin and nobody would dig.
Bring us something shiny that isn't iron, and maybe we'll listen.
Ye smell of smoke and fear, wee thing.
fairies.swat_line: You swat at a Frost Fairy. It dodges, laughing.
fairies.snow_line: A heap of snow drops on your head. You slog on slowly for a while.

economy.note: M8.6 (ADR 0015; user choices 2026-09-25). Coins are counted in copper. The copper-to-silver rate is a guess: the Book 1 text gives no rate.

rest.refused_line: It is too cold and open to sleep here. Find a roof or a camp.
rest.poor_line: You cannot pay for the room (%s).

hunger.hungry_line: You went to bed hungry. Your max HP is down %d%% until you eat.
hunger.fed_line: You eat at the inn after your work.

inn.note: M14.2 (ADR 0021). Patrons at Erin's inn, served by the player. Numbers are game balance, not canon. Book 1: the inn opens in 1.05; it is half blown up in 2.10T and rebuilt in 2.11. Early guests are mostly Drakes and Gnolls from Liscor.
inn.meal_line: It is %s time. Guests are coming to the inn: %d.
inn.left_line: A %s gives up waiting and leaves. The inn's name suffers.
inn.served_line: You serve %s to %s. You are paid %s.
inn.income_line: The inn took in %s from your serving today.

standing.note: M14.3 (ADR 0021). Relationships and reputation. Numbers are game balance, not canon. Reputation is +-cap; a town is the nearest settlement above a map's location, a faction is an NPC's canon faction.
bands: %s lights up when you come near.

brawl.note: M14.5 (ADR 0021). The player attacks an NPC (Brawl). Numbers are game balance, not canon. A major NPC (a pending canon event still needs them) gets a one-time fate warning; fate_delay is the seconds the Strike button stays off. act_seconds: how often a hostile NPC acts. attack: the first blow of the day; kill: the death (victim, witness: relationship with the player; town, faction: reputation).
fate_lines: %s has a part in what comes next.
Strike them down and the story will bend around the gap.
The System will not stop you. Do you go on?
